### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via OPEN (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/realtime-protocol.mdx`  _(via OPEN (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **16** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b2148cb74c9f30b0f7251bf32c51d1b6b8e4469c` — the merge of head `7f0e0e6fe72a685a8a9e3602e2d012fa2df46872` into base `258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b2148cb74c9f30b0f7251bf32c51d1b6b8e4469c && git checkout b2148cb74c9f30b0f7251bf32c51d1b6b8e4469c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275 7f0e0e6fe72a685a8a9e3602e2d012fa2df46872 && git checkout -B drift-repro 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275 && git merge --no-ff 7f0e0e6fe72a685a8a9e3602e2d012fa2df46872

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7f0e0e6fe72a685a8a9e3602e2d012fa2df46872`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.page-visibility-predicate-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.stored-listing.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/cel-has-argument.test.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/cel-has-argument.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.test.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.visibility-predicate-has-argument-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/view-walk.ts, packages/lint/src/page-walk.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/walk.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, .changeset/25168-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.md (precedent, on main)

Reviewed against ruling `6351260886` (letter A) on card #25281, the PR body, the 13-file net diff `origin/main...7f0e0e6fe` (+1088 / −29, matching the PR file list), and the 47 check-runs on the head: 36 `success`, 11 `skipped` (opt-in and conditional jobs), 0 failed. The ruling's 追认 by the maintainer is pending (see ③); this record judges the diff against the ruling as written.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing itself — right.** `validate-visibility-predicates.ts` arm (3b) (lines 1361–1390) refuses, at severity `error`, a `has()` call with exactly one argument whose AST node is not a `.` selection, reported at the same `where`/`path` as its siblings and only when the front end accepted the source (`!refusal`), exactly as ruling point 1 fixes it. Shapes: bare name, index as last step, and every other non-selection (`.?`, call, literal, operator) under one id `visibility-predicate-has-argument`.

2. **Oracle = the engine, mechanism (b) — right, and pinned.** `firstRefusedHasArgument` (lines 1028–1073) keys on `op === 'call' && args[0] === 'has' && args[1].length === 1 && arg.op !== '.'`, the same AST reading `indexedHasSelection` uses in `cel-engine.ts` (1557–1567). `rewriteIndexedHas` lowers every `.` argument whose chain root is not an identifier, so after it the only `has()` calls cel-js's macro still refuses as `has() invalid argument` are the non-`.` ones: equivalence by construction. Pinned both ways against `celEngine.compile`: 22 refused / 10 accepted shapes (`validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts` 1744–1790) and a three-way engine/door/listing set over 18 + 11 predicates (`…stored-listing.test.ts`). The PR's stated reason for (b) over (a) — one compile error per source would hide `has(status)` behind an unknown function — holds. A member call (`rcall`) is not matched; `has()` and `has(a, b)` are not this arm's (engine refuses under another message); a `has(` inside a string literal has no call node. `has(1.x)` passes the arm and compile refuses it for its TYPE — exactly the blind spot ruling point 2 keeps, and the spec test names it as such.

3. **The #16118 mask stays load-bearing — right.** `hasCallSpans` (917–936) masks every `has` call regardless of argument shape, so `has(status)` alone is ONE finding (this id) and `has(status) && status == 'x'` keeps `visibility-bare-identifier` on the unwrapped occurrence beside it; both pinned (1851–1856, acceptance pair 1724–1738). Ruling point 4 met.

4. **Prescriptions — right.** `hasArgumentHint` (1083–1108): bare name → `has(ROOT.x)` or `'x' in ROOT` with `CANONICAL_ROOT_BY_LAYER` (`record` runtime / `data` metadata); a bare ROOT (`record`, `current_user`) → a field OF it, never `record.record`, read off `SCOPE_ROOTS` + `VIEW_PAGE_EXTRA_ROOTS` so `type` is correctly not a root; index last → `size(e)` greater-than `i`, string key → `'k' in e`; `.?` → the plain selection; anything else → the one form. No null-guard text (pinned), one line ≤ 200 (pinned). Message quotes the engine's wording `has() invalid argument` and no tracker id. Ruling point 5 met.

5. **One non-blocking finding — the quoted argument can mis-slice in one exotic shape.** `spanText` (1003–1012) slices the author's `source` at the AST node's `start`/`end`, but `parseCelToAst` → `parseCelToAstWithReason` parses `rewriteNullableTernary(source)` (`cel-engine.ts` 794–808), which reserializes the source when a `cond ? v : null` ternary is present. In that shape the offsets index the reserialized text, so the `argument` quoted in the message and the `receiver`/`index` in the index hint can be wrong bytes. The VERDICT is unaffected (decided on `op`, not on text), the `bare` hint reads the name off the AST, and the only trigger is a null-branch ternary inside a visibility predicate, which has no sensible boolean reading. `hasCallSpans` guards the identical exposure with a `startsWith('has')` bail-out (930); `spanText` has only range checks. Direction is safe (right refusal, possibly off quote). Escalated in ③; not a FAIL.

6. **Save doors — right.** `runtime-gate.ts:1174` sorts findings by severity with no per-id allowlist, so the new `error` reaches `422 INVALID_METADATA` on the page and view doors without further wiring; pinned by the two new REFUSED rows and the view-door assertion in `runtime-gate.page-visibility-predicate-writes.test.ts` (95–97, 206–209).

7. **Public surface — right, nothing beyond the id.** `VISIBILITY_PREDICATE_HAS_ARGUMENT` exported from `packages/lint/src/index.ts`; `os explain` entry registered in `RULE_EXPLANATIONS`; `SCOPE_ROOTS` was already a formula export (`index.ts:38`), so no new formula surface. No docs page enumerates this rule family by id (tree grep for the sibling id hits only lint and metadata-protocol tests), so no `content/docs` edit is owed; `Flag docs affected by code changes` is green.

8. **ADR-0087 kit — right.** D3 entry `18.visibility-predicate-has-argument-refused.ts` carries id/surface/replacement/reason/acceptanceCriteria, no backticks in `surface`, registered by the directory concatenation `registry.ts.template` describes (1151); `check-adr-0087-registration` and the `refused-shapes.test.ts` registered-id list are green. Detector `visibilityHasArgument` (`refused-shapes.ts` 421–478): `toMajor: 18`, id equals the entry id, `detect(stack, report)` ignores #25279's third `context` parameter (type-compatible, as the PR says). It reads a bare string or `{ source }` envelope on `form` / `formViews.KEY` / `config` payloads (`mapViewPayloads` 586–637), `sections` + `groups` + `fields`, and page components through `mapPageComponents` (nested children via `mapComponentTree`) — the carriers the door's `formViewSites` / `walkPageComponents` judge. No D2 conversion, as ruling point 7 requires.

9. **Token reader `refusedHasArguments` — right as a LISTING reading.** Reviewed against the engine shapes: skips a member call (`.` or `.?` before `has`), string literals including raw, triple-quoted and escaped, zero- and multi-argument calls; strips grouping parens; an operator or `in` at depth 0 → `other`; `]` last → `index`; `.` + name last → selection; a lone non-literal name → `bare`. Held to the door and the engine three-way over 29 predicates on the lint side and 27 + 19 shapes in its own suite. The one asymmetry the PR concedes (a predicate that is also broken CEL may be listed while the door names its syntax fault first) is acceptable for a 需手动处理 listing.

10. **Two inherited listing-reaches-more asymmetries, neither new here.** (a) The spec walker visits source-authored (`html`/`react`) pages' derived region cache (`walk.ts:386`, deliberate) while lint's `page-walk.ts:80` skips them, so a stored source-authored page could be listed where the door gives no verdict — already the case for `viewDataApiProvider` (main:366). (b) A flat authored view with no `viewKind` is judged by lint's `self` site but the overlay case of `mapViewPayloads` needs `viewKind` — an authored-only shape, not a stored row. Recorded, not this PR's to fix.

11. **Pins rewritten, not silently — right (ruling point 6).** Module note: five gating rules, §Function existence point 2 → "exactly TWO axes", the CEL-TYPE blind-spot bullet, and a new §`has()` argument shape citing the ruling id. Test rows 898–926 flipped with the ruling cited; the "#13594 narrows this pin by exactly one axis" block → two axes with `has(status)` beside `totallyBogusFn(1,2)`. `cel-engine.ts` STILL OPEN bullet records that the page/view door now reports the argument while the first-error masking fact is unchanged.

12. **Ruling point 9 (⛔ Not) — none taken.** No `validateExpression` routing (the lint diff imports none); `@objectstack/formula` is comment-only (no engine semantics for `has(x)`); severity `error`, no warning tier; no console or render-side file touched.

13. **Premise (ruling point 8).** The dev reports 0 producers in HotCRM at `4166f21` and 0 in this repository at `5801a4f`, `premise_still_valid: true`. Within this brief's inputs the in-repo claim is consistent with the head tree (no CEL string carries either shape outside tests); HotCRM is the dev's measurement as reported, not re-measured here.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/25281-visibility-has-argument-refused.md`: `@objectstack/lint: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`; line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the changeset and the PR body; BREAKING banner with FROM → TO, Unchanged, and the one-line fix for an author; exactly one marker `adr-0087: registered visibility-predicate-has-argument-refused`, naming the entry id. Shape matches the #25168 → PR #25192 precedent (`.changeset/25168-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.md` on main). `Check Changeset`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-empty-changeset` all green on the head.
- **Right.** A value an author could write is now refused ⇒ `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, BREAKING, `minor` under the launch-window convention, as ruling point 7 and AGENTS.md's "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves" require. Both packages the diff moves are named.
- `@objectstack/formula` is not named: its diff is a docblock (`cel-engine.ts` 404–416); no export, type or behaviour moves, so under "moves" no line is owed, and the Require-a-changeset step is green. Flag for the seat only: if "anything that publishes" is read as emitted `.d.ts` bytes, a `patch` line for formula is the conservative add; not a defect.
- Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` — right. The accept set shrinks; nothing widens.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions: []`** — none to answer.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1** (object/flow/action/sharing-rule/hook surfaces already refuse both shapes through `validateExpression` but prescribe the generic "predicates are bare CEL"): answered — outside this card's surface by ruling point 9 (no routing through `validateExpression` either way), and the verdict there is right; "noted, not filed" is acceptable for a hint-text nit. The seat may file an S card if it wants the `has()` spelling there.
- **Deviation** (the PR body's attribution line links the card thread rather than the seat thread the dispatch named): cosmetic, no code effect; accepted.
- **Finding ①5 (`spanText` under a null-branch ternary)**: escalated to the adopting seat as non-blocking — accept as a measured cosmetic edge, or ask the dev for a one-line guard (quote `'its argument'` when `rewriteNullableTernary(source) !== source`, or a content check like `hasCallSpans` has). Either way the refusal is right.
- **Inherited listing asymmetries (①10)**: recorded; precedent-bound, not this PR's.
- **File surface**: `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts` and the runtime-gate writes test are the id's required wiring (export, `os explain`, save-door pin) inside "one new gating rule id in the existing family"; no breach of the ruling's surface. Serial constraint cleared as claimed: #25299 merged, not rebased; the three-dot diff holds the 13 files only.
- **追认 pending**: ruling `6351260886` is a proxy ruling under the maintainer's delegation, marked `auto-adjudicated` and reversible on one word. The maintainer's 追认 has not reached the card as of this record, and the PR is correctly draft. This verdict judges the diff against the ruling as written; it does not stand in for the 追认, and the PR must not leave draft before it arrives.
- **Check-runs**: 36 success / 11 skipped on `7f0e0e6fe`; the skipped jobs are opt-in or matrix-conditional (upgrade harness, packed-tarball smoke, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood shards). No gate family failed.

**VERDICT: PASS**
